A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SelfCite. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial layout changes and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SelfCite experiments on LongBench-Cite, including best-of-N sampling, SimPO training, ablations, iterative optimization, and a Claude Citations comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds an NLI-reward baseline, ALCE evaluations, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The context-ablation reward, citation-only best-of-N sampling, SimPO optimization, and length balancing remain unchanged. Expanded Algorithm 1 incorporates the 384-token filter already stated in v1's prose and clarifies candidate indexing; it does not establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds ALCE evaluation on ASQA and ELI5 (Appendix F, Table 8), extending sentence-level long-context evaluation to chunk-level citation tasks under a training-to-evaluation distribution and format mismatch. Existing LongBench-Cite coverage and training datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SimPO with NLI rewards, a controlled alternative initialized from LongCite-8B. The new ALCE comparison includes prompted Llama-2-13B-chat and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and reported results from Huang et al. (2024), with the latter explicitly distinguished by its in-distribution training. The Claude Citations comparison already existed in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces zero-shot ALCE evaluation using NLI-based citation metrics, ASQA exact-match recall, and ELI5 correctness. It also adds a controlled reward comparison and a latency protocol using eight A100 GPUs, batch size one, and model parallelism. These are additional protocols; the original LongBench-Cite settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether SelfCite's reward improves on an NLI reward with the training pipeline held fixed, whether sentence-level training transfers to chunk-level ALCE tasks, and how sampling versus reranking contributes to latency. Existing reward, length-balancing, training-size, iterative-training, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run performance estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same candidate-diversity statistic: 4.8 unique candidates per statement on average, with standard deviation 3.2. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds NLI-baseline results (75.0 average citation F1), ALCE results, and latency measurements, while retaining the original SelfCite Table 1 scores. Table 2 changes Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct average correctness without citations from 60.2 to 68.9 and with citations from 71.7 to 63.3. Table 4 changes the 8K-training F1 from 64.4 to 65.9 and citation length from 195.2 to 158.1. These reported revisions do not establish across-version model improvements.

T1.justification: The necessity/sufficiency reward derivation and Appendix B's ContextCite surrogate-model and citation-extraction mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Algorithm clarification and explicit restatement of the reward sum introduce no new theoretical result or mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: self-supervised context-ablation rewards improve fine-grained citations through best-of-N sampling and preference optimization. The headline improvement of up to 5.3 citation-F1 points remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the interpretation that ContextCite SFT reduces answer correctness with one of approximately preserved correctness, following revised baseline scores. It adds substantive discussion of the mismatch between contributive training and corroborative evaluation, qualifies ALCE comparisons by training conditions, interprets latency tradeoffs, and explicitly limits applicability to models exposing output probabilities.

D1.justification: v2 adds a SelfCite source-code link, specifies NLTK segmentation of ContextCite responses, documents the NLI model and its capped sentence-ablation procedure, and supplies latency hardware settings. Appendix A's original training recipe is largely unchanged; these additions mainly expand reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mudgal et al. (2024) to motivate best-of-N evaluation and expands positioning through Appendix G/Table 9, comparing citation granularity, generation passes, preference optimization, context capacity, and supervision. Most compared works and the central self-supervised positioning were already present in v1.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify citation resampling, simplify the SimPO rationale, and revise results interpretation and limitations. v2 adds an Impact Statement, a latency subsection, and Appendices E–G, moving the existing qualitative appendix to H. The overall narrative and main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column report to a two-column conference layout with different front matter, headers, and figure/table placement. v2 adds latency, ALCE, and prior-method comparison tables and expands Table 1. Existing figures and qualitative tables are retained but resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the reward's distinctive value: the controlled NLI comparison reports 75.0 versus SelfCite SimPO's 77.9 average F1, while ALCE transfer tests and latency measurements address generalization and practical cost absent from v1. Clearer applicability limits and code-access information also help. Some new prose overstates superiority: Appendix F's claim that LongCite beats prompting conflicts with the ELI5 citation scores in Table 8. This localized weakness does not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support.
